summary: Opaque quota waterfall causing sustained throttles during parallel preflight + chunked upload workflow
description: Issue summary: BrightMart reported repeated 429 throttles (tenant-level) during their nightly bulk sync job after enabling edge-proxy connection pooling and after a dedicated-pool autoscaler rollout. Impact: Nightly backfills fail intermittently, causing downstream sync retries and customer SLA alerts. Environment: Dedicated pool (BrightMart), prod-eu-west, workflow: preflight HEADs -> signed-url PUTs (parallel, chunked) -> websocket progress stream. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start BrightMart bulk-sync with concurrency 48, chunk size 8MB, preflight enabled. 2) Observe series of HEADs followed by parallel PUTs and immediate websocket connections for progress. 3) Watch for tenant-scoped 429s ~5-10 minutes into the run. Observed behaviour: Tenant-level token exhaustion resulting in sustained 429s that persist across requests for 7-20 minutes despite low CPU/GPU usage on dedicated nodes. Expected behaviour: Short-lived per-route spikes with rapid refill; no sustained tenant-wide exhaustion. Attachments: request sample IDs rqt-89f3/ rqt-89f4, logs (attached), dashboard links (rate-limiter ledger + tenant heatmap).
comments: 2024-10-15T15:12:00Z - Aisha Raman: Opening ticket. Customer reports 40-60% failure rate for nightly bulk sync; able to reproduce in their account when running at scale. Provided request IDs and example timestamps.

2024-10-15T15:48:00Z - Carlos Mendez (Support): Acked and began triage. Asked for: 1) exact start time of next failing run, 2) sample SDK client version, 3) whether signed-url refreshes are batched. Requested console logs and rate-limiter ledger export.

2024-10-15T17:05:00Z - BrightMart (Customer): Provided logs and confirmed they recently toggled edge-proxy connection pooling in front of Redwood ingress. Also noted an autoscaler change last week that altered dedicated-pool refill epoch window.

2024-10-16T09:35:00Z - SRE (Evan Cho): Investigating. Correlated tenant ledger: high volume of preflight HEADs were being counted under the same route weight as actual PUTs. Observed health-check probe cluster from orchestrator performing 100s of quick HEADs during the run window.

2024-10-16T11:12:00Z - Carlos Mendez (Support): Hypothesis: edge-proxy multiplex + connection-reuse is amplifying preflight fanout and causing token accounting to attribute preflight HEADs to primary route, driving token-bucket depletion. Also seeing refill epoch misalignment after autoscaler rollout causing delayed refill under load.

2024-10-16T14:40:00Z - Engineering (Maya Gupta): Deployed a ledger export and replayed request stream in a staging rate-limiter harness. Confirmed double-counting for multiplexed preflight flows when route tag absent. Proposed mitigation: tag preflight route as low-cost path and separate it into isolated burst pool; align refill epoch across edge and origin; add short-term burst credit increase for BrightMart.

2024-10-17T08:50:00Z - Carlos Mendez (Support): Applied temporary burst credit to customer and pushed config change: route_isolation=true for preflight route, increased dedicated pool burst by 2x for 2 hours. Customer confirmed bulk-sync completed successfully.
2024-10-18T10:05:00Z - BrightMart (Customer): Confirmed stable nightly run for two consecutive days after changes. Requested guidance to avoid recurrence.
2024-10-18T10:30:00Z - Carlos Mendez (Support): Closing loop with recommended permanent config and follow-ups. Marking ticket Resolved.
investigation_notes: Ledger analysis showed a sawtooth pattern: large blocks of HEAD requests counted as token usage identical to PUTs between 02:00 and 02:20 UTC.
Edge proxy connection pooling caused single client to open fewer connections but multiplex many logical preflight messages resulting in mis-tagged route classification at ingress.
Autoscaler rollout changed dedicated-pool refill epoch from 60s aligned windows to an offset schedule; under bursty fanout this delayed effective refill by up to 45s causing prolonged exhaustion.
Reproduced locally by replaying customer request sequences in staging rate-limiter harness; enabling route tag prevents HEADs from consuming PUT bucket.
No evidence of node resource exhaustion or OOM on serving runtime; problem is quota accounting and configuration rather than serving throughput limits.
resolution: Temporary: granted emergency burst credits to BrightMart and set route_isolation=true for their preflight route; increased dedicated pool burst capacity during their nightly window. Permanent: engineering implemented route tagging to ensure preflight HEADs count against an isolated lightweight bucket and aligned refill epoch for the dedicated pool edge/origin path. Customer advised to stagger preflight/signing refresh by 5s across workers and to use the recommended SDK concurrency limiter. Monitoring: new ledger metric (per-route preflight_token_ratio) added to Console dash and alerting rule created.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4321: Add unit & integration tests for multiplexed preflight accounting (assigned to eng-rate-limiter)
Create KB article for customers: 'Design patterns to avoid tenant-level quota waterfalls for multipart uploads' and link in Console guidance (owner: DevRel)
Add automated audit to detect dedicated-pool refill-epoch drift after autoscaler changes (owner: infra)
Recommend customer-side: stagger worker startup by 3-7s and enable route_isolation on heavy preflight endpoints
